source.title: MHC Interp #1: Previous-Token Heads Become Attention Sinks Under Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections

page_placements.theme: Identifying induction heads: scores miss heads or diverge from causal role

record.file_problem: The text refers to appendix images that are not represented in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: It tests induction-head behavior with behavioral probes, ablation, and path patching in mHC, mHC-lite, and non-mHC models, rather than reproducing the original training and measurement setup.
record.gate_note: The study reports qualitative induction-head and previous-token-head findings. Probe prompts and ablation setup are described but are not outcome rows by themselves. The logit-lens results concern a different measure and are not included.
record.test_reason: The study trains 781M mHC, mHC-lite and standard residual models on Dolma. It reports induction heads in all three, found with stripe scores and confirmed by ablation and path patching. This is a result on universality (V4) in a new architectural setting, not a replication of the original method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author finds that induction heads look and behave similarly across mHC, mHC-lite and residual models but sit in earlier layers. Previous-token heads in mHC models look sink-like and need behavioural methods to identify them. The author also notes that heads in mHC models can carry several roles.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains 781m mHC, mHC-lite, and non-mHC models with four residual streams and uses behavioral probes, ablation, and path patching. The text does not specify a direct replication recipe for the original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported previous-token-head appearance and detection differ between mHC and mHC-lite; the text also says the method used to obtain doubly stochastic matrices affects how residual streams work.

fits_no_version.finding: Previous-token heads in mHC models look like attention sinks with high kurtosis or verticality. Stripe detection fails for them, and ablation is needed to find them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Constrained hyper-connection architectures change how previous-token heads look and how they can be detected.

fits_no_version.finding: Induction heads and previous-token heads sit in earlier layers in the mHC variants than in the residual model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The residual connection architecture shifts which layers induction heads occupy.

record.problems: Results about induction and previous-token heads are qualitative, with no reported head IDs or numerical behavioral scores. The text gives no number of independent training runs, and the cited appendix images are not represented in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant reported outcomes were left out. The logit-lens accuracy and KL results concern other measures.

untested.parts: No small attention-only models. No test of composition between induction heads and previous-token heads.
Only one size (781M), one dataset and one training run per variant. No other model families or modalities.
No measure of in-context-learning loss by token index.
Data properties are not varied and formation over training is not tracked.
Few-shot task learning is not studied.

record.verdict_notes: Informal LessWrong post. One run per architecture, no numerical induction scores or head IDs, and appendix figures are not in the text. Tranche changed from T2 to T3: this is a new-architecture setting, not a different method aimed at the original question. The V1 label was removed because the system type does not match V1.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports induction-head behavior, but does not test whether induction heads form by composing with an earlier previous-token head. The models are not described as small attention-only transformers.
No training-time trajectory, abrupt formation window, in-context-learning gain, or training-loss bump is measured.
No large-transformer in-context-learning loss-by-token-index measure or estimate of how much ICL induction heads carry.
Only mHC, mHC-lite, and non-mHC variants at the stated scale are reported; multiple sizes, training runs, model families, architectures beyond these variants, and modalities are not tested.
The study compares final models with different connection methods, but does not measure when heads form during training, vary data properties, or test whether ICL persists.
Few-shot task learning and alternative mechanisms for it are not tested.
No training-time sub-steps or overlapping transitions are measured.
